column3: Directly repeats spouses from yourselves and adds children, showing the generative outcome of the pairing named in the focus.
Blessings upon the Prophet do not clarify creation, pairing, divine incomparability, or perception.
Adam's creation from dust by the command brings a concrete instance of God's unconditioned creative power.
It portrays God making the earth habitable and bringing forth diverse plant pairs, extending the focus's ordered creation.
The warning about taking protectors besides God supports exclusive reliance but adds little to the focus's creation claims.
It identifies God as the one who originated the speaker, supplying a personal instance of the focus's cosmic creatorship.
It closely joins human mates, livestock pairs, and successive womb creation, directly expanding the focus's paired and multiplying creatures.
God's power to make one community instead concerns mercy and judgment, not the focus's created pairs.
Its instruction to the People of the Book does not illuminate the focus's claims about creation or divine uniqueness.
It repeats God as Originator of the heavens and earth and adds knowledge of the unseen and seen.
God's knowledge of the unseen and seen complements the focus's hearing and sight, though it adds no account of pairing.
The pairing of the blessed with heavenly companions uses marriage language in a distinct eschatological setting.
It explains the human pairs as a source of repose, affection, and mercy, adding their relational purpose.
It asserts that God alone is the protecting ally, gives life to the dead, and has power over all things.
It calls God Originator of the heavens and earth while contrasting the messengers' humanity with their Creator.
It names God Creator of everything and rejects rival creators whose creations could be confused with His.
God's possession of all in the heavens and earth supplies the sovereign setting for the focus's creative acts.
The Creator of the heavens and earth is able to create humans again, emphasizing the scope of His creative power.
Its worldly enjoyments of different groups do not clarify the focus's pairs or divine attributes.
The cosmic upheaval condemns a theological claim but does not itself explain the focus's creative order.
It says God dispersed humanity through the earth, directly complementing the focus's statement that He multiplies people.
It explicitly states that God created humans in pairs, a central claim of the focus.
The preceding verse assigns all disputed judgment to God and returns to Him, supporting His sole lordship.
Its paired varieties of punishment do not clarify created spouses or divine incomparability.
Its human analogy denies equal partnership in what one owns, supplying a boundary analogy for God's incomparable status.
The revelation formula and divine names establish the surah's authority but add little to the focus's specific claims.
It identifies the male and female pair as God-made from human origin, directly specifying human pairing.
It names God Originator of the heavens and earth and rejects taking another protector besides Him.
Its denunciation of calling on female idols does not clarify the focus's created pairs or attributes.
It states that God created all pairs and made livestock available for riding, closely matching two elements of the focus.
It repeats God as Originator of the heavens and earth and says He increases creation as He wills.
The angels' praise and forgiveness in the cosmic setting add only indirect context to the focus.
It treats crops and livestock as God-created and rebukes assigning shares of them to false partners.
It presents livestock as a divine provision for riding and food, adding their practical role after their mention in the focus.
The call to justice and the shared lordship of God provide surah context but do not explain creation or pairing.
Human responsibility for one's striving has no substantive connection to the focus's claims.
It classifies livestock as carrying and furnishing animals, a limited elaboration of their created presence.
Noah's grateful descendants do not clarify creation, pairs, or divine attributes.
The heaven splitting at the fulfilled promise does not add to the focus's creative order.
It details dwellings and materials supplied from livestock, extending the creaturely benefit of the livestock named in the focus.
The warning of the Day of Gathering belongs to the same surah but does not clarify the focus's claims.
Its two kinds of fruit in each garden share only a broad pairing motif.
God's hearing and knowledge of every utterance in heaven and earth complements the focus's hearing and sight.
God's ownership of the heavens and earth and gift of daughters or sons extends His creative disposal of human life.
Its three eschatological classes are called pairs or groups, not the generative pairs in the focus.
It affirms God's true judgment over powerless rivals and closes with the exact attributes Hearing and Seeing.
Individual guidance and responsibility do not add to the focus's creation, pairing, or divine uniqueness.
It calls God the Lord of the heavens and earth who originated them, directly confirming the focus's opening claim.
Its inherited dietary distinctions about livestock do not clarify their creation or the focus's pairs.
The immediate continuation gives God the treasuries of heaven and earth and control of provision.
Its denial of protectors or helpers besides God offers only a limited exclusivity parallel.
It names God as Hearing and Seeing while describing a divine sign shown to His servant.
Later sectarian division after knowledge does not clarify the focus's creative or attributive claims.
It depicts the mate made from one self and follows conception, adding a human reproductive sequence.
Joseph addresses God as Originator of the heavens and earth and as his guardian in this life and the next.
Its assertion that divine play would come from God's own presence only indirectly marks the Creator's transcendence.
Abraham's exclusive appeal to the one who originated him supplies a brief personal counterpart to the focus.
It invokes God as Hearing and Seeing against arrogant disputation, reinforcing those attributes in a polemical setting.
The shared religion of the prophets provides surah context but not a direct explanation of the focus.
The pairing of souls at judgment is distinct from the biological and livestock pairs of the focus.
It describes God dispersing varied colors and kinds across the earth, complementing the focus's ordered multiplication.
Its reward for faith and affection for kin does not clarify the focus's claims.
The rule of proportional retaliation does not illuminate creation, pairing, or divine attributes.
God's making night and day for rest and livelihood broadly parallels purposeful ordering for creatures.
It asks who begins and repeats creation and provides from heaven and earth, rejecting any deity alongside God.
The messenger's denial of foolishness does not clarify the focus's creation or divine uniqueness.
God's hearing and knowledge occur in a dispute over belief, offering only a limited attribute parallel.
The scene of enduring punishment does not clarify creation, pairs, or divine incomparability.
It grounds worship in the one who originated the speaker and to whom all return.
The parable of a powerless man and one commanding justice does not clarify the focus.
The language of prophetic messengers and God's guidance does not add to the focus's claims.
The believers' trial before entering Paradise does not clarify creation or divine attributes.
Its household eating permissions do not illuminate the focus's created spouses or livestock.
God's ownership of heaven and earth and the return of all affairs offer a broad, already established surah frame.
It repeats humanity's dispersal on earth and return to God, but earlier candidates already supplied this link more directly.
The inheritance ruling does not clarify the focus's creation, pairs, or attributes.
Moses leading his people from darkness to light does not illuminate the focus's claims.
God's power over all things broadly supports creative omnipotence but adds no specific focus element.
Its condemnation of false revelation and the death scene do not clarify the focus.
The modes of God's communication with humans only indirectly support the distinction between Creator and creature.
It presents the God-given human disposition and the unchanging order of God's creation.
Human failure to see and hear supplies a contrast to God's hearing and sight, without explaining them.
Reviving dead land as a sign of emergence does not clarify the focus's pairs or divine incomparability.
The splitting sky does not explain the focus's creative order or attributes.
The denial of the Prophet's control leaves judgment to God, a limited sovereignty parallel.
The believers' restraint and forgiveness do not clarify the focus's claims.
Abraham directs himself to the Originator of the heavens and earth and rejects association with others.
The food of the punished does not illuminate creation, pairing, or divine attributes.
It identifies God as Creator of the heavens and earth and rejects another deity alongside Him.
The warning from earlier peoples and God's lack of injustice does not clarify the focus.
The imagined ransom of all on earth does not clarify the focus's creative order.
It explicitly names the male and female pair, but this point has already been supplied by earlier direct candidates.
God's witnessing of all things offers only a distant parallel to the focus's divine perception.
The proportional recompense of deeds does not clarify the focus's claims.
The detailed pilgrimage rules do not illuminate creation, pairing, or divine attributes.
The wrongdoing of those who deny signs does not clarify the focus's content.
The clothing and modesty rules do not explain the focus's created pairs or divine uniqueness.
Its possible replacement with other wives uses spouse language but does not concern their creation or purpose.
The divine witness and revelation argument only broadly supports God's authoritative knowledge.
The sexual ethic's reference to spouses does not clarify the focus's creation of pairs.
It joins creation from one self, the mate made from it, and the spreading of many men and women, directly filling the focus's human-pair and multiplication sequence.
It calls God Originator of the heavens and earth, denies that He has a companion, and affirms His creation and knowledge of everything.
It distinguishes God from created sight while affirming that He sees all sight, directly sharpening the focus's closing attribute.
It states that God made pairs of every fruit, extending the focus's ordered pairing from people and livestock to the earth's produce.
Its question whether a creator is like one who does not create supplies a direct boundary for the focus's declaration of divine incomparability.
The joined heavens and earth, life from water, and divine separation broaden the focus's account of cosmic creation.
It attributes human origination and the faculties of hearing and sight to God, closely complementing the focus's final attributes.
It makes God the creator of every living creature and displays diversity of animal forms, extending the focus's mention of livestock.
It declares God's sole dominion, rejection of offspring and partners, and creation of all things in measure.
It describes humanity's creation from water and the making of blood and marriage relations, adding a direct social consequence of created pairing.
It traces human creation from dust to humanity spreading through the earth, closely complementing the focus's multiplication claim.
The diversity of languages and colors presents further ordered difference within the Creator's signs.
It says God perfected everything He created and began human creation from clay, adding a distinct account of human origin.
It attributes the human spirit and the faculties of hearing and sight to God, furnishing a creaturely counterpart to the focus's attributes.
It combines human creation from dust and fluid, creation in pairs, and gestation under God's knowledge.
It glorifies the Creator of all pairs, including what the earth grows, humans, and what they do not know.
It states that God created livestock for people and made them subject to human possession and use.
It explicitly affirms that God created both people and what they make, extending the focus's universal creatorship.
It describes God making the earth a dwelling, the sky a structure, and human forms excellent, expanding the focus's creative setting.
It traces human creation through dust, fluid, gestation, birth, maturity, and death under God's direction.
It explicitly joins God's gift of male and female offspring with His will over fertility, adding the sexed and generative outcomes of creation.
It states that God created all things in pairs, giving the focus's pairing language its widest formulation.
It specifies the reproductive source from which the male and female pair is created.
It challenges humans to recognize the Creator who brought them into being, reinforcing the focus's creative claim.
It joins creation of the heavens and earth in truth with the fashioning of human forms.
It says God produced humanity and gave hearing, sight, and hearts, directly complementing both the focus's multiplication and final attributes.
It appeals to the grandeur due to God as Creator, supporting the focus's exalted portrayal of Him.
It describes God creating people in successive stages, supplying another account of ordered human formation.
It recalls human creation from a humble fluid, adding a concrete origin for the people whom God multiplies.
It names God as the one who created, proportioned, and balanced the human being, adding order within human creation.
It affirms that God assembled humans in whatever form He willed, underscoring His unrestricted formative power.
It directs the human being to consider the source from which he was created, supporting reflection on divine origination.
It identifies that human origin as a flowing fluid, supplementing the focus's statement of divine multiplication.
It explicitly names God's creation of the male and female pair, a concise direct counterpart to the focus.
It affirms the human being's creation in the best form, adding a qualitative dimension to divine formation.
It identifies human creation from a clinging substance, another direct account of human origin.
It declares God uniquely one, directly supporting the focus's denial that anything is like Him.
It explicitly states that none is comparable to God, the closest concise parallel to the focus's incomparability clause.
